title: Sharp Studio
oneLiner: Browser-based image lab—filters and transforms you can tweak, fork, and extend in the UI.

problem.heading: Problem
problem.description: Most lightweight image tools are either opaque presets or heavyweight editors. Developers and designers wanted a middle ground: immediate feedback on filters and geometry, readable code paths, and room to experiment without leaving the tab.

myRole.heading: My role
myRole.description: Built the React surface and Canvas rendering loop: input handling, filter graph composition, and state so adjustments stayed responsive on mid-range laptops. Focused on keeping the draw path predictable for future plug-in style extensions.

solution.heading: Solution
solution.description: Shipped Sharp Studio as a single-page app that treats the canvas as the source of truth for pixels, with React orchestrating controls and history. Exposed parameters as first-class UI so "hackable" meant users could see cause and effect, not buried sliders.

impact.heading: Impact
metrics: ⚛️ React + Canvas split: smooth UI without jank on mid-range hardware
🖼️ Entirely client-side—no upload dependency for core workflows
🔧 Extension-friendly filter hooks without rewriting the renderer
impact.description: A portfolio-grade playground that shows how I reason about performance-sensitive UI, not just forms and dashboards.
